To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the literature on presence is diverse in its conceptualizations and operationalizations of presence; (2) there are many potential sources of presence, including the medium itself, the user, and the environment; (3) there are many different ways to assess presence, including self-report, behavioral, and physiological measures; (4) the literature suggests that presence is multidimensional; and (5) presence is related to other constructs such as parasocial interaction, social presence, and immersion

(a) presence is a perceptual illusion of "being there," "feeling there," and/or "doing there" in a mediated environment, (b) presence is an individual phenomenon, (c) presence is a multidimensional construct, and (d) presence is measured by a standardized instrument.

presence is a perceptual illusion of the existence of a person or object in a particular location, when in fact that person or object is not there.

presence is an emergent phenomenon that results from the complex interplay of the user's physical and social context, the characteristics of the medium, and the characteristics of the content (e.g., Lombard & Ditton, 1997).
